traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Ruppiaceae: leaves usually whorled, sometimes alternate or opposite; leaves simple; margins serrate or entire; veins single; blades linear; stipules absent; leaf rosettes none; plants hermaphrodite; ovary superior; stems herbaceous; flowers in racemes, in spikes or in umbels, rarely solitary; flowers actinomorphic; perianth absent; fruit aggregate; stamens 2; carpels (2-) 4 (-16). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.
